Thought: In gas chromatography, the retention time of a molecule is influenced by its boiling temperature. Molecules with lower boiling points tend to vaporize more readily and travel through the column faster, leading to shorter retention times. Conversely, an increase in boiling temperature generally means the molecule will vaporize less readily and take longer to travel through the column, resulting in a longer retention time. Therefore, an increase in boiling temperature of the analyzed molecule typically results in an increase in retention time.
